# GridDragScroll's monitor outlives a native drag from the grid body

## Context

A consumer grid declares a `nativeDragZone` (`Neo.component.Base#nativeDragZone_`, filled by `Neo.main.addon.NativeDragSource`) so a row can be dragged as an HTML5 drag into content the synthetic pipeline cannot reach — here an editor iframe. The same grid keeps the default drag-to-scroll (`Neo.grid.ScrollManager#dragScroll` → `Neo.main.addon.GridDragScroll`). The operator reported (2026-09-02): drag a row onto the editor, drop, move the pointer back over the grid — the grid still shows the `grabbing` cursor and scrolls under a plain mouse move, no button pressed.

Reproduced in real Chromium against that grid, read off `Neo.main.addon.GridDragScroll` and a document-level event witness:

| moment | `monitorDrag` | `activeDrag` | body cursor | events seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| after the press + first moves | **true** | false | `''` | `dragstart` on the row cell |
| after the drop | **true** | false | `''` | `dragend` — no `mouseup` |
| pointer moved back over the grid, no button | false | **true** | **`grabbing`** | — |

## The Problem

`GridDragScroll#onDragStart` (its `mousedown` handler, `src/main/addon/GridDragScroll.mjs:257-283`) arms a **monitor** on every left press over a registered body: `monitorDrag`, a `delay` timer, and document-level `mousemove` / `mouseup` listeners that wait for `minDistance` to start a drag-scroll. `NativeDragSource` arms the row `draggable` on the same press and the browser starts a native drag on the next moves. From `dragstart` on, the browser delivers **no** `mousemove` and **no** `mouseup` to the page — only `drag*` events — so the monitor never sees its release. `dragend` fires; the addon does not listen to it. The monitor survives the whole drag and the drop.

The next ordinary pointer movement over the document then reaches the stale monitor listener: elapsed time and distance from the original press both qualify, `onMonitorMove` calls `startDrag`, and a drag-scroll runs with no button held — `document.body.style.cursor = grabbing !important`, document `mousemove`/`mouseup` listeners attached, the view scrolling under the pointer until some later `mouseup` arrives. The `neo-draggable` exclusion at `:239-243` does not help: `NativeDragSource` arms `draggable` lazily on the first move, so at press time the row is neither `neo-draggable` nor `draggable`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/addon/GridDragScroll.mjs` — `construct` binds `onDragStart`/`onMonitorEnd`/`onMonitorMove` (`:80-83`); `onDragStart` arms the monitor (`:257-283`); `onMonitorMove` starts the drag when delay + distance are met (`:289-300`); `onMonitorEnd` clears the timer, the monitor and its listeners (`:307-316`); `onDragEnd` retires an active drag, restores the cursor and starts the kinetic tail (`:127-…`); `unregister` already ends an active drag by calling `onDragEnd({type: 'mouseup'})` (`:410`) — the precedent for ending without a real event. The addon has no `dragstart` / `dragend` awareness at all.
- `src/main/addon/NativeDragSource.mjs` — document-level capture listeners for `mousedown` (arm), `dragstart` (fill `DataTransfer`), `dragend` + `mouseup` (disarm) (`:110-118`); its class doc states the browser suppresses `mouseup` during a native drag (`:174`). Since PR #18091 it stamps `neo-native-drag-active` on `body` for the drag's lifetime.
- `src/grid/ScrollManager.mjs` — registers the view with the addon on mount (`updateDragScrollAddon`); `dragScroll_` defaults to `true`, so every grid has the monitor.
- Component fixture with a real native drag: `test/playwright/component/apps/empty-viewport` lists `NativeDragSource` in `mainThreadAddons`; `test/playwright/component/component/NativeDragZone.spec.mjs` drives `dragstart`; `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-focus` (the grid click-focus fixture) has a long scrollable grid and an outside button.

## The Fix

1. `GridDragScroll` listens for `dragstart` on the document (capture, bound once in `construct`) and treats it as the end of any pointer gesture it is tracking: a live `monitorDrag` → `onMonitorEnd()`; a live `activeDrag` → `onDragEnd({type: 'mouseup'})` (the `unregister` precedent — cursor restored, listeners removed, no kinetic tail from a drag the user did not release). The browser guarantees no further mouse events for that gesture; the addon must not wait for one.
2. The `dragstart` listener lives on the document, not on registered bodies: the native drag may start on a row inside a registered body or on a foreign `draggable` — either way the monitor is dead. Registration count does not gate it; a page without grids pays one no-op listener.
3. Witness in `test/playwright/component/grid/`: the `grid-focus` fixture gains `NativeDragSource` and a `nativeDragZone` on the long grid (`delegate: '[data-record-id]'`, one `text/plain` type). Arms: (a) press on a row, move past `minDistance` so `dragstart` fires, continue outside, release → `monitorDrag` and `activeDrag` are `null`, `body.style.cursor` is empty — red on `dev` (`monitorDrag` survives); (b) then move the pointer over the long grid with no button → `activeDrag` stays `null`, the view's `scrollTop` does not change — red on `dev` (a phantom drag-scroll starts); (c) control: a plain press-move-release on the same grid without a native drag still scrolls it (the drag-scroll itself keeps working).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 `GridDragScroll` ends a live monitor and a live active drag on a document `dragstart`; no other behaviour of the addon changes.
- [ ] AC-2 Witness arm (a): after a native row drag and drop, the addon holds no gesture state and the body cursor is restored — red-first on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-3 Witness arm (b): a button-less pointer move over the grid after that drop neither starts a drag-scroll nor scrolls the view — red-first on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-4 Witness arm (c): ordinary drag-to-scroll on the same fixture still scrolls (control green before and after).
- [ ] AC-5 `components` + `unit/manager`/`unit/grid` suites green at head; `NativeDragZone` component spec unchanged and green.

## Out of Scope

- Whether the drop into the consumer's editor iframe resolves — that is the frame's drop handler and the payload protocol (`cnetDragZone` in the consumer), not the engine's gesture state; this ticket ends where the engine's own stuck state ends.
- Touch gestures: a `touchstart` press never turns into a native drag.
- #17889 (pointer-event sensors for `DragDrop`) — a different addon and pipeline.

## Avoided Traps

- **Listening to `dragend` instead of `dragstart`.** `dragend` arrives only after the drop, so the monitor would still be armed during the whole drag; and a source node removed mid-drag never fires `dragend` (Mnemosyne's finding on #18091). `dragstart` is the moment the browser stops talking to us; end the gesture there.
- **Excluding `draggable` nodes at `mousedown`.** `NativeDragSource` arms `draggable` after the press, so the row is not draggable when the monitor is armed; a path check cannot see a drag that has not been declared yet.
- **Running the kinetic tail on the phantom end.** `onDragEnd` computes a fling from the drag history; ending an `activeDrag` on `dragstart` must not fling the grid — pass through the same `{type: 'mouseup'}` path `unregister` uses and let the empty recent history yield zero velocity, or cancel the animation explicitly.

## Related

- #18065 / PR #18066 — the other `GridDragScroll` mousedown finding of the day (the cancelled default).
- PR #18091 (#18087) — `NativeDragSource` stamps `neo-native-drag-active` for the drag's lifetime; a second signal the addon could read, but `dragstart` is the primary one.
- #17889 — drag sensors to Pointer Events (adjacent, different pipeline).
